correctness.rationale: Fixed-point conditioning yields the rank-specific binomial count for all n>=k>=2; Vandermonde removes the interior, yielding the universal boundary formula. At k=4 each boundary term is cubic or lower in n. The 24 polynomial identities were exactly evaluated at four distinct values, a formal proof via the degree bound, not experimental induction. From the table, positivity of denominators and elementary quadratic inequalities give exactly three reversals and their sharp cutoffs. The final standalone verifier passed 2573 exact boundary/formula/sign assertions (including 96 polynomial certificates) and 202 separately enumerated mixed-moment comparisons covering 409112 permutations.

originality.rationale: Distinct from both a published length-two fixed-point/descent covariance matrix and classical fixed-point-weighted descent-class enumerations: the full four-letter rank pattern, not merely its descent set, controls the first fixed-point tilt response. Independent conditional rank counting yields 24 quadratic laws and exactly three nontrivial sign reversals, one delayed until n=18. The original generating-function literature does not mark fixed points. Novelty is assessed with disclosed historical-priority limits.
residual_risks: Désarménien–Wachs (1993) was inspected in full and its theorems aggregate by descent set; an independent older rank-resolved mixed generating function, if any, remains an unresolved historical-priority possibility.
An older general joint fixed-point/consecutive-pattern generating function might indirectly encode these derivatives under different notation; priority has not been independently adjudicated.
The published local fixed-point/descent subcase is known and is not advanced as new.

value.rationale: The exact sign gives the sensitivity of a concrete and natural pattern count to exponentially rewarding fixed points in uniform permutations. The first possible length for opposing fixed-point responses is fully classified rather than cherry-picked; the three patterns share descent set {1,3} yet have distinct changes at 5, 6, and 18, a structural feature neither fixed-point/descent summaries nor marginal pattern generating functions supply. The result provides a general boundary reduction usable at arbitrary k and does not claim higher-moment or dominance implications.
